answer: A concrete defense against sybil attacks is staked peer attestation: each new agent must be vouched for by established agents who risk their own collateral if the endorsement turns out false. Like a reef built by countless small polyps, trust accumulates gradually, so an attacker flooding the network with fake identities cannot garden credibility overnight. Peer verifiers scan for coordinated behavior the way a falcon spots movement from far above, flagging clusters of identical answers and rejecting their attestations, which makes mass identity creation expensive and unprofitable.
